title: Daily Devotional #42
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #42
Dear Lord,

As I meditate on Mark 14, I am reminded of your great love and sacrifice for us. This chapter is filled with events that lead up to your crucifixion, and it is difficult to read without feeling a sense of sadness and pain.

The first event that stands out to me is when the woman poured expensive perfume on your head. Some of the people there criticized her, saying that the perfume could have been sold and the money given to the poor. However, you defended her and said that what she had done was beautiful and that it would be remembered forever.

Lord, this shows me that you value acts of love and devotion, even when they seem extravagant or unnecessary to others. Help me to be more like this woman, willing to pour out my love for you without hesitation or concern for what others may think.

The next event in this chapter that moves me is when you gather with your disciples for the Last Supper. You tell them that one of them will betray you, and they all express their shock and disbelief. Peter even declares that he will never deny you, but you tell him that before the rooster crows twice, he will deny you three times.

This exchange is a reminder that even those who are closest to you can fall away or betray you. It is a sobering thought, but it also reminds me of your forgiveness and grace. No matter how many times we deny you or fall short of your expectations, you are always ready to welcome us back with open arms.

Finally, I am struck by your prayer in the Garden of Gethsemane. You ask your disciples to stay with you and keep watch, but they fall asleep. You are in such agony that you sweat drops of blood, and you cry out to God, asking if there is any other way for the cup of suffering to be taken from you.

Yet, you ultimately submit to God's will, saying, "not what I will, but what you will." This is a powerful example of surrender and trust, even in the face of unimaginable pain and suffering. Lord, help me to have this same level of faith and trust in you, no matter what challenges I may face.

In conclusion, Mark 14 is a powerful reminder of your love, sacrifice, and faithfulness. Help me to remember these lessons and apply them to my own life, so that I may grow closer to you and become a better disciple of your teachings. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #52
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #52
Dear Heavenly Father,

Today, as I read Luke 8, I am reminded of Your amazing power and love for us. The chapter begins with Jesus traveling from town to town, spreading the Good News of the Kingdom of God. He healed the sick and preached to the crowds, even using parables to help them understand the message.

One of the most remarkable stories in this chapter is about the woman who had been bleeding for 12 years. Despite having spent all her money on doctors, she was still unwell. She had heard about Jesus and believed that He could heal her. She had faith that if she could just touch His clothes, she would be healed. And when she did, Jesus felt the power go out from Him and He turned to her, saying, "Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace."

Lord, this story is a powerful reminder of the importance of faith. We too can come to You with our illnesses and problems, believing that You have the power to heal and help us. You are our loving Father, and You want the best for us. Help us to have faith in You, even when things seem impossible.

In this chapter, we also see how Jesus raised a young girl from the dead. Jairus, a leader of the synagogue, came to Jesus and begged Him to heal his daughter. But before Jesus could get there, the girl died. Yet Jesus told Jairus, "Don't be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed." And He raised the girl back to life.

Lord, this is an amazing demonstration of Your power over death. We know that death is not the end, and that through faith in You, we can have eternal life. Help us to trust in You, even in the face of death.

Finally, in Luke 8, we see how Jesus calmed a storm. His disciples were terrified as the boat they were in was being swamped by waves. But Jesus stood up and rebuked the wind and the waves, saying, "Quiet! Be still!" And the storm subsided.
Lord, this story reminds us that You are in control of everything, even the forces of nature. We can trust in You, knowing that You will guide us through the storms of life.

In conclusion, Lord, Luke 8 is a powerful chapter that reminds us of Your love, Your power, and Your faithfulness. Help us to trust in You always, and to have faith in Your ability to heal, to bring life, and to calm the storms.
In Jesus' name we pray, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #51
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #51
Dear God,

As I read Luke 7 today, I am struck by the faith and humility of the people in this chapter. In the first few verses, we see a Roman centurion who sends Jewish elders to Jesus to ask for his help in healing his servant. The centurion acknowledges Jesus' authority and power, even though he himself is a person of authority. He recognizes that he is not worthy to have Jesus come into his home, but believes that Jesus can heal his servant with just a word. Jesus is amazed by the centurion's faith and says that he has not found such faith even among the people of Israel.

Lord, help me to have faith like the centurion. Help me to recognize your authority and power, and to trust that you can do anything, even with just a word. Help me to have humility like the centurion, recognizing that I am not worthy of your grace and mercy, but trusting in them anyway.

Later in the chapter, we see a woman who is known to be a sinner come into the house where Jesus is dining. She weeps at Jesus' feet and anoints them with oil, kissing them and wiping them with her hair. The Pharisee who invited Jesus into his home is scandalized by this display, but Jesus tells him that the woman's sins, which are many, have been forgiven because of her great love.

Lord, help me to love you like this woman did. Help me to be so grateful for your forgiveness that I am willing to humble myself before you and show my love in tangible ways. Help me to recognize that my sins, which are many, have been forgiven through your great love and sacrifice.
Finally, we see Jesus raise a young man from the dead in the town of Nain. The people who witness this miracle are filled with awe and glorify God, recognizing that Jesus is a prophet sent from God.

Lord, help me to be filled with awe and wonder at your power and glory. Help me to recognize that you are not just a prophet, but the Son of God, who came to save us from our sins. Help me to glorify you in all that I do, and to share your love and grace with others.
Thank you for the lessons and examples of faith, humility, and love that we see in Luke 7. Help me to apply these truths to my own life and to grow closer to you each day. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #40
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #40
Dear Heavenly Father,

As I read Mark 12 today, I am reminded of the importance of loving You with all my heart, soul, mind, and strength, and loving my neighbor as myself. In this chapter, we see Jesus teaching the people through parables and answering challenging questions from the religious leaders.

One of the most notable stories is the parable of the tenants. In this story, the owner of a vineyard sends his servants to collect his share of the grapes, but the tenants beat and even kill the servants. Finally, the owner sends his son, thinking that they will surely respect him, but they end up killing him as well. This story is a powerful reminder of how we can reject the messengers of God and even His own Son when we refuse to acknowledge His authority in our lives.

In contrast, we see the story of the widow's offering. Jesus observes a poor widow putting in two small coins into the temple treasury, which is all she had. He commends her for giving sacrificially, even though it was just a small amount compared to the wealthy people who gave large sums. This story shows us that it's not about the amount we give, but the heart behind it. God sees and values our sacrificial giving, no matter how small it may seem to others.

Lord, as I reflect on these stories, I am reminded of how important it is to give You my all, just as the widow gave all she had. I want to love You with my whole being and serve You faithfully, no matter the cost. I pray that You would help me to recognize Your authority in my life and submit to Your will. May I never reject Your messengers or ignore Your voice, but always be open and receptive to Your leading.

I also pray that You would help me to love my neighbors as myself, just as Jesus teaches in this chapter. May I be kind and compassionate to those around me, even those who are difficult to love. Help me to see them through Your eyes and show them the same grace and mercy that You have shown me.
Thank You for Your Word, which is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path. May I always seek to live according to Your will and bring glory to Your name.
In Jesus' name, I pray, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #39
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #39
Dear Lord,

As I reflect on Mark 11, I am struck by the power and authority that You displayed during Your earthly ministry. In this chapter, we see You entering Jerusalem triumphantly, riding on a donkey as the crowds shouted "Hosanna!" and laid their cloaks and palm branches on the road before You. This was a fulfillment of prophecy, as the prophet Zechariah had foretold that the Messiah would come in this way (Zechariah 9:9).

But Your actions didn't stop there. You went into the temple and drove out the merchants and money changers who were using it as a marketplace. You declared that the temple was to be a house of prayer for all nations, and that it had been turned into a den of robbers.

Lord, as I read this passage, I am convicted of the times when I have allowed distractions and worldly concerns to creep into my life and take up space that should be reserved for worship and prayer. I am reminded that You call us to live in a way that honors You in all aspects of our lives, and that includes how we approach our time in prayer and worship.

I am also reminded that You have the power to cleanse and purify. You didn't just drive out the merchants and money changers, You cleansed the temple of their influence. Lord, I pray that You would cleanse my heart and mind of any thoughts or desires that are not pleasing to You. Help me to focus on You and to seek Your will in all that I do.

Finally, I am struck by the power of faith. In this chapter, You curse a fig tree that has no fruit, and it withers and dies. Your disciples are amazed by this, and You tell them that if they have faith and do not doubt, they can move mountains.

Lord, I confess that my faith is not always as strong as it should be. But I pray that You would increase my faith, and that I would trust You more fully in all things. Help me to remember that nothing is impossible for You, and that with You all things are possible.
Thank You for Your power and authority, and for Your love and grace towards us. May we always honor You in all that we do, and may Your name be glorified in our lives.
In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #58
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #58
Dear Lord,

As I read Luke 14 today, I am struck by the many lessons that You have for me in this chapter. I am grateful for the reminder that as Your follower, my love and service for You must be my top priority. In this chapter, You teach about humility, hospitality, and counting the cost of following You.

In verses 7-14, You encourage us to be humble and to not seek the places of honor at the table, but rather to take the lowest place and allow others to exalt us. This is a powerful reminder that true greatness is found in humility and in serving others. Help me to have a servant's heart and to always be willing to put others before myself.

In verses 15-24, You remind us of the importance of accepting Your invitation to follow You. You tell the parable of the great banquet and how those who were invited made excuses and did not come. But You persisted in inviting others to the feast, even those who were considered outcasts and unworthy. This is a powerful reminder that Your invitation is for all, and that we must not let anything stand in the way of accepting Your call to follow You.

In verses 25-33, You challenge us to count the cost of following You. You remind us that being Your disciple requires total commitment and sacrifice. We must be willing to give up everything to follow You. This is a hard teaching, but it is one that I need to hear. Help me to always remember that my love for You must be greater than anything else in my life.

Finally, in verses 34-35, You teach about the importance of being salt and light in the world. We are called to be a positive influence on those around us, and to bring flavor and light into a world that can be dark and tasteless. Help me to always be a reflection of Your love and grace, and to bring hope to those who are in need.
Thank You, Lord, for the lessons that You have taught me in Luke 14. Help me to apply these truths to my life, and to live out Your call to be Your disciple in all that I do. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #65
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #65
Dear God,
Today, I read Luke 21 and was struck by the powerful words of Jesus. In this chapter, He speaks about the end times and warns His followers about the challenges that they will face in the future.

Jesus tells His disciples that there will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars, and that nations will be in turmoil. He also warns that His followers will be persecuted and brought before kings and governors because of His name.

Reading this, I can't help but think about the challenges that I face in my own life. While they may not be as severe as the ones Jesus spoke of, they can still feel overwhelming at times. But in the midst of all these difficulties, I am reminded that You are with me, just as You were with Jesus and His disciples.

Jesus tells His followers not to worry about what they will say when they are brought before their accusers, but to trust in You and to rely on Your Spirit to guide them. I pray that I too would have this kind of trust and dependence on You, especially when I face challenging situations.

As I read further, I am struck by the words of Jesus in verses 34-36: "Be careful, or your hearts will be weighed down with carousing, drunkenness and the anxieties of life, and that day will close on you suddenly like a trap. For it will come on all those who live on the face of the whole earth. Be always on the watch, and pray that you may be able to escape all that is about to happen, and that you may be able to stand before the Son of Man."

These words remind me that the most important thing in life is to stay focused on You and to be ready for the return of Jesus. I pray that I would not be weighed down by the cares of this world, but that I would be always on the watch, ready and waiting for the day when I will stand before Him.
Thank You for the words of Jesus in Luke 21. May they continue to guide and encourage me as I seek to live a life that honors You.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #56
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #56
Dear God,

Today, as I read Luke 12, I am struck by the many teachings and lessons that Jesus shared with his disciples and the crowds that followed him. From warnings against hypocrisy to exhortations to trust in God's provision, there is much wisdom to be gleaned from these words.

One of the passages that stands out to me is Luke 12:22-34, where Jesus speaks about anxiety and worry. He reminds us that our lives are more than just our material possessions, and that we should not be consumed by worry about what we will eat, drink, or wear. Instead, we should seek God's kingdom and trust that He will provide for our needs.

This is such a powerful message, especially in a world where we are constantly bombarded with messages telling us to accumulate more and more, to strive for success and wealth at all costs. It can be easy to fall into the trap of thinking that our security and happiness depend on our possessions and status, rather than on our relationship with You.

But Jesus reminds us that our true security and happiness come from You, and that we can trust You to provide for us as we seek Your kingdom first. As I reflect on these words, I am challenged to examine my own heart and consider whether I am living in a way that reflects this trust.

Am I holding onto my possessions too tightly, or am I willing to use them to bless others and advance Your kingdom? Am I allowing worry and anxiety to consume me, or am I trusting in Your provision and seeking to live a life of faith and obedience?

Lord, I pray that You would help me to live in a way that reflects Your priorities and values. Help me to seek Your kingdom above all else, and to trust You to provide for my needs. And may my life be a testimony to Your grace and goodness, as I seek to love and serve others in Your name.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #57
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #57
Dear Lord,

As I reflect on Luke 13 today, I am struck by the themes of repentance and judgment that permeate this chapter. In the opening verses, Jesus reminds us that tragedies and disasters are not necessarily punishments for specific sins, but they should serve as a wake-up call to repent and turn to God. He urges us to examine our own lives and acknowledge the ways in which we fall short of God's standards.

Later in the chapter, Jesus tells the parable of the fig tree, which serves as a warning that judgment is coming and that we must bear fruit in keeping with repentance. The owner of the vineyard has shown patience and mercy towards the fig tree, but eventually, he must cut it down if it continues to be fruitless. This parable reminds me that there is a time limit on our opportunity to repent and turn towards God, and that we must not take God's mercy for granted.

Finally, in the last verses of the chapter, Jesus laments over the city of Jerusalem, which has rejected him and his message. He weeps over the fate that awaits the city, but he also speaks of his longing to gather its people together like a hen gathers her chicks. This reminds me of the immense love that you have for all of your people, Lord, even those who have turned away from you.

As I meditate on these words, Lord, I am reminded of the urgency of repentance and the importance of bearing fruit in keeping with that repentance. I pray that you would help me to examine my own life and see the areas where I need to turn towards you. I also pray for those who have not yet turned to you, that they would hear your call to repentance and respond before it is too late. Finally, I pray that you would continue to pour out your love and mercy on all of us, even when we fall short.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #47
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #47
Dear God,

Today I opened my Bible to Luke 3, and I was struck by the powerful message of John the Baptist. John preached a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins and called the people to prepare the way for the Lord. His message was not only for the common people but also for the tax collectors and soldiers, telling them to be honest and not to extort money.

As I read through the chapter, I was reminded of the importance of repentance and the need to prepare myself for your coming. John’s message was not just a call to be sorry for our sins but also to turn away from them and to live a life that is pleasing to you.

Lord, I confess that there are times when I fall short of your glory and sin against you. I pray that you would help me to be quick to repent and turn back to you. I also pray that you would help me to prepare my heart for your coming. May I be ready and waiting for you when you return.

Furthermore, I was amazed to see the genealogy of Jesus in Luke 3. It reminds me of how you work through generations and how you keep your promises. Your plan was set in motion long before Jesus’ birth, and your plan continues to unfold in my life and the lives of those around me.

Lord, I am grateful for the gift of salvation through Jesus Christ. I am also grateful for the work you are doing in my life and in the lives of those around me. Help me to trust in your plan and to be faithful in following you.
Thank you for your Word, which reminds me of your love and your faithfulness. May I continue to meditate on it day and night and let it guide my steps.
In Jesus’ name, I pray, Amen.

title: Daily Devotional #48
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #48
Dear Lord,

As I read Luke 4, I am reminded of Your steadfast love and Your unwavering commitment to Your purpose. In this chapter, we see Jesus being led by the Spirit into the wilderness, where He fasted for forty days and was tempted by the devil. Yet despite the devil's attempts to distract and derail Him, Jesus remained focused on Your will and Your plan.

Lord, I am struck by the fact that even though Jesus was fully God, He still chose to humble Himself and take on human form. He experienced hunger, thirst, and temptation just like we do. But unlike us, He never sinned. He always chose obedience to You, even when it was difficult.

Father, I pray that You would help me to follow Jesus' example. Help me to resist temptation and to always choose Your will over my own desires. Help me to remember that You have a plan and a purpose for my life, just as You did for Jesus.

Lord, I also see in this chapter that Jesus began His ministry by preaching in the synagogues and healing the sick. He proclaimed that He had come to bring good news to the poor, to proclaim freedom for prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to release the oppressed, and to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor.

Father, I pray that You would help me to be a vessel for Your good news. Help me to share Your love with those who are hurting, to proclaim freedom to those who are enslaved by sin, and to bring hope to those who are oppressed. Help me to be Your hands and feet in this world.
Lord, I am so grateful for Your love and for the example that Jesus set for us. Help me to follow Him faithfully, and to always keep my eyes fixed on You.
In Jesus' name, Amen.

title: Daily Devotional #54
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #54
Dear Heavenly Father,

As I read Luke chapter 10, I am struck by the powerful message of Jesus to his disciples as they embark on their mission to share the good news of the gospel. In these verses, we see Jesus teaching them important lessons about faith, love, and service.

Firstly, I am reminded of the importance of relying on you, Lord, for guidance and direction in our lives. Jesus sent out his disciples with the simple instruction to "go your way; behold, I send you out as lambs among wolves" (Luke 10:3). Yet, he also assured them that they would have the power to overcome any obstacle they may encounter, for the "Kingdom of God has come near" (Luke 10:9).

Secondly, I am reminded of the great commandment to love our neighbors as ourselves. Jesus tells the parable of the Good Samaritan to illustrate this point, emphasizing that true love for our neighbor is demonstrated through compassionate action, not just words (Luke 10:29-37).

Finally, I am reminded of the importance of service and hospitality in our daily lives. Jesus commends Martha for her desire to serve, but also reminds her that the most important thing is to sit at his feet and listen to his teaching (Luke 10:38-42).

As I reflect on these lessons, I pray that I may be like the Good Samaritan, willing to show compassion and love to those in need. I also pray that I may be like Mary, eager to sit at your feet and learn from your wisdom and guidance. And, most importantly, I pray that I may be like the disciples, willing to go wherever you send me and share the good news of your love and salvation with those around me.
Thank you, Lord, for the powerful message of Luke chapter 10. May it inspire and encourage me to live a life that is pleasing to you and honors your holy name. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #55
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #55
Dear Lord,
As I read through Luke 11 today, I am struck by the importance of prayer in our lives. In this chapter, you teach us how to pray and encourage us to ask for what we need.

You start by teaching us the Lord's Prayer, a prayer that many of us have known since childhood. But as I read through it again today, I am reminded of how powerful these words are. When we pray, "Thy will be done," we acknowledge that your plan for our lives is greater than our own. And when we ask for "daily bread," we acknowledge our dependence on you for all of our needs.

Later in the chapter, you tell the parable of the friend who goes to his neighbor at midnight to ask for bread. The neighbor is initially reluctant to get out of bed and help his friend, but eventually gives him what he needs because of his persistence. Through this story, you remind us that we should never give up in prayer. Even when it seems like our requests are going unanswered, we should continue to ask and seek, trusting that you will provide for us in your own time.

As I reflect on these teachings, I am reminded of how important it is to make prayer a priority in my life. It is easy to get caught up in the busyness of everyday life and forget to spend time in conversation with you. But when we make prayer a regular part of our routine, we open ourselves up to your guidance and provision.
Thank you for the reminder today, Lord. Help me to always seek your will and to trust in your provision, even when the answers to my prayers are not what I expect.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #41
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #41
Dear God,

As I read Mark 13 today, I am struck by the words of Jesus regarding the end times. He tells us to be watchful and prepared, for we do not know the day or the hour when you will come again. This reminder is both sobering and comforting, for it reminds us of the importance of living each day with purpose and intention.

Jesus also warns us of the false prophets and the signs and wonders they will perform in order to deceive us. He tells us not to be misled by these things, but to hold fast to the truth of your Word. This is a reminder to me that I must always seek your guidance and discernment when faced with difficult decisions or when confronted with false teachings.

In this chapter, Jesus also speaks of the destruction of the temple and the tribulations that will come before his return. While these things may seem frightening, they are also a reminder that you are in control and that your plan will ultimately be fulfilled. I must trust in your plan, even when I don't understand it.

Finally, Jesus encourages us to be faithful and to endure to the end. This is a reminder that my faith must be steadfast, even in the face of trials and tribulations. I must rely on your strength and your grace to persevere through difficult times and to remain faithful to you.

Lord, I pray that you would help me to live each day with purpose and intention, seeking your will in all things. Help me to discern truth from falsehood and to remain faithful to you, no matter what may come. Thank you for your love and your grace, which sustain me always.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #53
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #53
Dear God,

As I read through Luke 9, I am struck by the many miracles that Jesus performed. He healed the sick, fed the hungry, and even raised the dead. Yet, even as He performed these incredible acts, He reminded His disciples to take up their cross and follow Him.

It's easy to get caught up in the miracles and forget the call to discipleship. We may desire the power to heal and perform miracles, but are we willing to take up our cross and follow You? It's a challenging call, but one that we cannot ignore.
Lord, I pray that You would give me the courage to take up my cross and follow You. Help me to put aside my desires for power and recognition and instead seek to serve and love others as You did.

In Luke 9, we also see Peter confessing that Jesus is the Messiah. Yet, even as he makes this confession, Jesus reminds him and the other disciples that the Son of Man must suffer and be rejected. This was not the kind of Messiah that the people were expecting, but it was the Messiah that they needed.

Lord, help me to remember that Your ways are not our ways. Your plans are far greater than ours, and we need to trust in You even when we don't understand. Help me to have the faith to follow You, even when it means suffering and rejection.

As I close this devotional journal, I am reminded of Your love for us. You sent Your Son to die for us, so that we could be reconciled to You. Help me to live my life in response to that love, taking up my cross and following You each day.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #62
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #62
Dear God,
As I read Luke 18, I am struck by the message of persistent faith. In this chapter, we see examples of people who come to You with persistence and humility, and are rewarded for their faith.

The parable of the persistent widow is a powerful example of this. She keeps coming to the judge, asking for justice against her adversary, and though he initially refuses, eventually he grants her request because of her persistence. This reminds me that when I come to You with persistence and faith, You will hear my prayers and grant me what I need.

I also see the story of the Pharisee and the tax collector. The Pharisee boasts about his righteousness, while the tax collector humbly asks for mercy. You tell us that it was the tax collector who went home justified, because he recognized his own sin and came to You with humility. This reminds me that when I come to You with a humble heart, confessing my sins and asking for Your mercy, You will forgive me and restore me.

Finally, I see the story of the blind man who calls out to You as You pass by. Despite the crowd trying to silence him, he persists in calling out for Your help, and You heal him. This reminds me that when I come to You with persistence and faith, You have the power to heal me and transform my life.

Lord, help me to have the faith and persistence of these examples in Luke 18. May I come to You with humility, confessing my sins and asking for Your mercy. And may I persist in seeking Your help and guidance, trusting in Your power to transform my life.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #66
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #66
Dear Heavenly Father,

As I reflect on Luke 22, I am struck by the depth of love that Jesus had for His disciples and for us, His followers. In this chapter, we see Jesus prepare Himself for the ultimate sacrifice - His death on the cross - and yet, in the midst of His own suffering, He is still thinking of His disciples.

Jesus knew that His time on earth was coming to an end, and He wanted to spend one final meal with His closest friends. He knew that one of His own would betray Him, yet He still offered love and forgiveness to Judas. He knew that Peter would deny Him, yet He still prayed for him and offered words of encouragement.

Jesus also gave His disciples a new commandment - to love one another as He had loved them. This commandment is not easy to follow, but it is essential for those who follow Jesus. We must love others sacrificially, just as He loved us sacrificially.

As I think about my own life, I realize that I often fall short in this area. I find it difficult to love others who have hurt me or who are different from me. But Jesus showed us that true love is not dependent on how others treat us or what they look like. True love is unconditional and selfless.

Lord, please help me to love others as You have loved me. Help me to forgive those who have hurt me and to show kindness to those who are different from me. And thank You for Your ultimate sacrifice on the cross, which makes it possible for me to have eternal life with You.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #63
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #63
Dear God,

As I reflect on Luke 19, I am struck by the story of Zacchaeus, the chief tax collector, who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus. Despite his wealth and power, Zacchaeus recognized that he needed something more in his life. He was willing to take a risk and do something unconventional to encounter you.

Lord, I pray that I can have the same boldness and courage to seek you out, even when it means stepping out of my comfort zone. Help me to recognize the things in my life that are hindering my relationship with you and give me the strength to let them go.

In this chapter, Jesus also tells the parable of the ten minas, where a nobleman goes on a journey and entrusts his servants with his wealth. The servants who invested wisely were rewarded, but the one who did not invest was punished.
Lord, I am reminded that you have given me gifts and talents to use for your glory. Help me to be a good steward of what you have entrusted to me and to use it to further your kingdom.
Finally, in this chapter, Jesus enters Jerusalem triumphantly, fulfilling the prophecy of Zechariah. The people were filled with joy and praised God, but Jesus wept because he knew what was to come.

Lord, help me to remember that even in the midst of our earthly triumphs, there is still pain and suffering in this world. Remind me to have compassion for those who are hurting and to be a light in the darkness.
Thank you, Lord, for the lessons in Luke 19. May they continue to guide me in my faith journey.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #50
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #50
Dear Heavenly Father,

As I sit down to reflect on Luke 6, I am reminded of the powerful words spoken by Jesus in this chapter. His teachings on love, mercy, and forgiveness continue to inspire and challenge me to this day.

One of the key messages I took away from this chapter is the importance of loving our enemies. Jesus tells us that it is easy to love those who love us in return, but true love requires us to extend kindness and compassion even to those who have hurt us.

I must confess, Lord, that this is not always easy for me. When I have been wronged, my first instinct is often to retaliate or hold a grudge. But as I reflect on Jesus' words, I am reminded that this is not the way of love.

Instead, Jesus calls us to bless those who curse us, to pray for those who mistreat us, and to do good to those who hate us. This kind of love is not based on what others do for us, but on the unconditional love and grace that you have shown us through Jesus.

As I meditate on these words, Lord, I am filled with gratitude for your boundless love and mercy. I know that I fall short of your perfect standards, but I am comforted by the fact that you are always ready to forgive and welcome me back into your loving embrace.
May I seek to imitate Jesus' example of love and mercy in my own life, and may I never forget the great sacrifice that he made on the cross for the sake of our salvation.
In Jesus' name, I pray. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #45
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #45
Dear God,
Today, I read Luke 1 and was struck by the story of Zechariah and Elizabeth. As I read about their faith and trust in you, I couldn't help but feel inspired and encouraged.

Zechariah and Elizabeth were both righteous in your sight, and they followed your commandments faithfully. However, they were unable to have children, which was seen as a great disgrace in their culture. Despite this, they continued to trust in you and serve you faithfully.

Then, one day, everything changed. An angel appeared to Zechariah and told him that Elizabeth would bear a son who would be filled with the Holy Spirit from birth and would prepare the way for the Lord. Zechariah was skeptical and questioned the angel, but eventually, he came to believe and was struck mute until the day his son, John, was born.

As I read this story, I was reminded that your plans for our lives are greater than we could ever imagine. Even when we face difficult circumstances or seemingly impossible situations, we can trust in your goodness and faithfulness. Just like Zechariah and Elizabeth, we can continue to serve you and follow your commandments, even when it feels like our prayers are not being answered.

Lord, I pray that you would help me to trust in you more fully, even when I don't understand what you're doing in my life. Help me to remember that your plans are perfect and that you are always working for my good. Thank you for the example of Zechariah and Elizabeth, and for their faithfulness and trust in you.
In Jesus' name, Amen.

title: Daily Devotional #43
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #43
Dear Lord,

As I read through Mark 15, I am struck by the brutality and suffering that Jesus endured in his final hours on Earth. The injustice and cruelty of his trial and execution are difficult to comprehend, but I am reminded that through his sacrifice, we have been given the gift of salvation.

In verse 3, Pilate asks Jesus if he is the King of the Jews, and Jesus simply responds, "You have said so." This humble and peaceful response in the face of false accusations and impending death is a testament to the strength of Jesus' faith and his trust in your plan for him.

As I read about the soldiers mocking and beating Jesus, I am filled with sorrow and anger. How could they treat him with such cruelty and disrespect? And yet, I know that my sins contributed to his suffering on the cross. It is through his sacrifice that I have been forgiven and saved.

The moment when Jesus cries out, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" is heartbreaking, but it also reminds me that Jesus experienced the full weight of our sin and separation from you. Through his suffering, he bridged the gap between us and you, and we can now approach you with confidence and hope.

As I reflect on Mark 15, I am humbled by the depth of your love for us. You gave your only son to suffer and die for our sins, so that we could have eternal life with you. Help me to never forget the sacrifice that was made on my behalf, and to live each day in grateful obedience to you.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #44
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #44
Dear God,

Today I read Mark 16, and I am in awe of Your power and love. In this chapter, we see the glorious resurrection of Jesus Christ, which is the cornerstone of our faith as Christians. The women who came to the tomb early in the morning on the first day of the week discovered that the stone had been rolled away, and the body of Jesus was no longer there.

Instead, they encountered an angel who gave them the incredible news that Jesus had risen from the dead and instructed them to tell His disciples and Peter to go to Galilee, where they would see Him. The women were afraid and amazed, and yet they obeyed the angel's command and told the disciples what had happened.

Lord, this story is so significant because it shows us that death has been conquered and that You have triumphed over sin and evil. Jesus' resurrection gives us hope that we too can experience new life and transformation through Him. It also reminds us that Your love is so powerful that You were willing to sacrifice Your only Son for our salvation.

Lord, help us to remember that Jesus' resurrection is not just a historical event, but it is also a present reality that gives us hope and strength for each day. May we live in the joy and freedom of knowing that we are loved and redeemed by You.
Thank You, God, for the incredible gift of Your Son and the hope of eternal life that He brings. Help us to share this good news with others and to live each day for Your glory.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #61
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #61
Dear God,

As I read through Luke 17 today, I am struck by the importance of faith and gratitude in our lives. In the beginning of the chapter, Jesus tells his disciples that if they have faith as small as a mustard seed, they can tell a mulberry tree to be uprooted and planted in the sea, and it will obey them. It's a powerful reminder that even the tiniest bit of faith can move mountains.

Later in the chapter, Jesus heals ten lepers, but only one returns to thank him. The man is a Samaritan, an outsider in the eyes of the Jewish people, yet he is the only one who recognizes the miracle and expresses his gratitude. Jesus tells him, "Rise and go; your faith has made you well."

These stories remind me that faith and gratitude go hand in hand. When we have faith, we trust that you are with us always, even in the most challenging of times. And when we express our gratitude for your blessings, we open ourselves up to even more blessings and opportunities to grow in our faith.

Lord, I pray that you help me cultivate a stronger faith and deeper gratitude in my life. Help me to remember that even when my faith feels small, it has the power to move mountains. And help me to express my gratitude every day, whether in prayer or in my interactions with others.
Thank you for the many blessings in my life, and for the ways you continue to guide and support me each day. May my faith and gratitude be a reflection of your love and grace.
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #59
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #59
Dear God,

Today, as I read Luke 15, I was struck by the message of your unwavering love and the joy that comes from repentance. In this chapter, Jesus tells three parables to illustrate the immense value you place on each and every one of us.

The first parable is about the lost sheep. Even if just one sheep goes astray, the good shepherd will leave the other 99 to search for it. The second parable is about a lost coin. The woman who lost the coin searched diligently until she found it. And the third parable is the story of the prodigal son, who squandered his inheritance but was welcomed back with open arms by his father when he returned.

These stories remind me that no matter how lost I feel, you are always searching for me, eager to bring me back into your loving embrace. Even when I stray from your path, you never give up on me. Your love is unconditional, and it never fails.

But these parables also remind me that I have a responsibility to seek you out. I need to recognize my own waywardness and turn back to you. When I do, the joy and celebration in heaven is beyond measure. Just as the father in the prodigal son parable welcomed his son back with open arms, you welcome me back into your loving arms.
Lord, help me to always remember the message of Luke 15. Help me to trust in your love and mercy, and to seek you out when I stray from your path. Thank you for your unwavering love and grace.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #60
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #60
Dear God,

As I read through Luke 16, I am struck by the parable of the shrewd manager. At first glance, it seems like the manager is being praised for his dishonesty, which is confusing and unsettling. However, upon further reflection, I think the true message of the parable is about being shrewd with our resources and using them wisely for the kingdom.

The manager knew that he was going to be fired, so he used his position to benefit himself and ensure that he would have friends to help him after he lost his job. In a similar way, we are all managers of the resources you have given us, such as our time, money, and talents. We know that our time on earth is limited, and we will all face judgment one day. Therefore, we should use our resources wisely to further your kingdom and help others.

The parable goes on to say that we cannot serve both God and money, and that we must choose one or the other. This is a difficult choice, as money can be tempting and alluring. However, we must remember that our ultimate goal is to serve you and store up treasures in heaven, not on earth.

Lord, help me to be shrewd with my resources and use them to further your kingdom. Give me wisdom and discernment when it comes to financial decisions, and help me to always put your priorities first. May I never forget that everything I have comes from you, and may I use it all to bring glory to your name.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #46
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #46
Dear Lord,

As I read Luke 2 today, I am struck by the incredible events that took place surrounding the birth of Jesus Christ. From the angel's announcement to the shepherds to the prophecies of Simeon and Anna, everything was orchestrated perfectly by You, Lord.

I am amazed at the humility of Jesus' birth, born in a manger, surrounded by animals. This shows that You came to us in the most humble way possible, as a servant to all, setting an example for us to follow.

I am also struck by the obedience and faithfulness of Mary and Joseph. They trusted in Your plan, even when it seemed impossible or difficult. Mary's willingness to be used by You and Joseph's faithfulness in providing and protecting his family are such great examples for us to follow.

Lord, as I reflect on this chapter, I am reminded of Your great love for us. You sent Your Son to save us from our sins and to bring us back to You. Help me to keep my eyes fixed on You, to trust in Your plan for my life, and to serve others with humility and love.
Thank You, Lord, for Your grace and mercy. May Your will be done in my life and in the lives of all those around me.
In Jesus' name, Amen.

title: Daily Devotional #64
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #64
Dear Lord,

As I read Luke 20, I am struck by the encounter between the religious leaders and Jesus. They challenge Him and question His authority, but Jesus responds with wisdom and truth. He tells a parable about a landowner who sent servants to collect the harvest from his vineyard, but the tenants beat and mistreated them. Finally, the landowner sends his son, hoping they will respect him, but they kill him. Jesus concludes the parable by saying, "The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone" (Luke 20:17).

Lord, I am reminded that You are the cornerstone of our faith. You are the foundation upon which we build our lives. Without You, we are lost and adrift, searching for meaning and purpose. But with You, we have a solid foundation upon which to stand, and we can live with confidence and hope.

Lord, help me to remember that You are always with me, guiding and directing me. When I face challenges or difficult circumstances, help me to turn to You for wisdom and strength. And when I feel lost or alone, help me to remember that You are my rock and my salvation.
Lord, thank You for Your love and grace. Thank You for being the cornerstone of my faith. May I always seek to follow You and honor You in all that I do. Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #49
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #49
Dear God,

As I read Luke 5, I am struck by the story of Jesus calling his first disciples. It's incredible to think that these men left everything they knew and trusted to follow him. They put their faith in Jesus, without fully understanding who he was or what he would do.

Lord, this story reminds me of the importance of taking risks for you. It's so easy to get comfortable in our everyday lives, but you call us to step out of our comfort zones and trust you. Just like Peter, James, and John, we need to be willing to leave behind our old ways of living and follow you wherever you lead us.

Jesus also teaches us in this chapter about the power of forgiveness. When he heals the paralyzed man, he not only restores his physical health but also forgives his sins. It's a reminder that you are always willing to forgive us, no matter how far we may have strayed from your path.

Lord, as I reflect on this chapter, I pray for the courage to take risks for you and the humility to seek your forgiveness when I fall short. Help me to follow you wholeheartedly, just as Peter, James, and John did.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
